g.text: RootCanal: How to trace BLE Link-Layer PDUs (and HCI) with Wireshark
What the built-in sniffers cover - and what they don't
emit BLE Link-Layer PDUs in a
format Wireshark natively dissects out of the box.
Below are the three built-in tracing options and exactly
Option A - HCI sniffer - HCI layer (Wireshark-native)
wrap HciSocketTransport in HciSniffer per host,
(4-byte direction + H4 type byte + HCI payload)
Wireshark "Analyze -> Decode As" auto-dissects HCI H4.
You see HCI_LE_* commands/events, ACL data and L2CAP.
This is HCI, NOT the on-air LL PDUs.
Option B - Baseband sniffer - BR/EDR only
BLE LL PDUs are NOT captured by this option.
Option C - Sniffer device - LL packets to log, not pcap
register a Sniffer Device on the LE phy
every LL packet whose src/dst matches
Great for seeing which LL PDUs flow on the virtual air
and in which direction, but only to the console/logs -
Option D - RAW LE LL PDUs via the LE Phy TCP port - custom framing
This port is served by LinkLayerSocketDevice.
Each message frame = 4-byte little-endian length prefix
A client connected here is itself a PhyDevice on the LE
phy: it can OBSERVE every LL PDU the controllers exchange,
and can even INJECT LL PDUs back.
length prefix (uint32 LE) + LL packet bytes
(these are RootCanal's OWN LL PDU encodings:
LLCP=0x41, ACL, ISO...). Wireshark does NOT parse
You must write a converter of your own:
1. capture via Option D (LE phy port)
2. translate each RootCanal LinkLayerPacket into the
Bluetooth LE LL PDU byte layout,
Then Wireshark dissects ADV_IND, SCAN_REQ, CONNECT_IND,
To get true BLE on-air LL PDUs dissected in Wireshark
True BLE LE LL PDU pcap
